facts.text: TEGA Thermal Gas Analyzer was deployed at Vastitas Borealis during Phoenix in 2008.

An array of eight single-use miniature vacuum ovens paired with a magnetic-sector mass spectrometer. The ovens heated soil and ice samples up to 1,000°C to measure the vaporized gases released at specific mineral decomposition temperatures.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Detected water vapor liberated at 0°C and carbon dioxide released at 725°C, confirming the presence of calcium carbonate (chalk) formed in liquid water.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Vastitas Borealis.
Demonstrated that the Martian arctic once experienced liquid water that reacted with carbon dioxide in a warmer, thicker ancient climate.
